subject: Horizon Pilot — access checklist, success criteria & owners
messages:
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: marta@horizonai.com
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Horizon Pilot — kickoff + access checklist

Hi Marta — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single checklist to work from. Action items below are split into pilot success criteria, access items we need from you, and what Redwood will deliver.

Pilot success criteria (proposal)
- Functional: Redwood model returns coherent responses for Horizon knowledge base queries with >90% precision on the sample prompts you shared.
- Perf: 95th-percentile inference latency <200ms for single-request path during 1–2k RPS bursts; average latency target ≤120ms for steady-state.
- Cost/scale: support ~100k tokens/day for the evaluation window.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 summary in place and confirmation of no long-term customer data retention for trial tokens.

Access & provisioning we need from Horizon
- SSO invites (SAML/Okta) for three engineers: marta@horizonai.com, eng+pilot@horizonai.com, and kevin@horizonai.com (please confirm these are the correct accounts).
- IP allowlist (CIDR or fixed IPs) so we can pin the pilot ingress and avoid auth friction.
- A small test dataset or sample prompts (anonymized) so we can pre-warm caches.

What Redwood will provide
- Temporary API key (14-day expiry) scoped to the pilot project and limited quota; sample curl examples.
- SOC2 summary and short security FAQ (we'll attach).
- An onboarding session next week to walk your engineers through integration and monitoring.

Proposed timeline
- Today: confirm SSO accounts and IPs.
- EOD (Redwood): temp API key provisioned.
- +2 business days: SOC2 summary and success-criteria workbook shared.
- Kickoff call: Tue/Wed next week (I'll send a calendar invite).

Please reply with any adjustments to the success criteria and the three SSO accounts + the IP ranges you want whitelisted. If that all looks OK I'll start internal tasks and loop in Aditya for key provisioning and Ben for the SOC2/retention answers.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

—
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0196

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the clear recap — this matches our notes. A few quick clarifications and asks from our side:

Success criteria tweaks
- Latency: 95th-percentile <250ms is acceptable for the pilot (our infra is a bit spiky).
- Scale: start with 25k tokens/day for the first 3 days, then ramp to 100k tokens/day as we validate.

Security/questions
- Please send your SOC2 summary and the short security FAQ. We need to confirm whether request payloads are stored and for how long.
- Do you have a dedicated private deployment option if we need it later? Not required for pilot but good to know.

Access we can provide now
- SSO accounts to invite: marta@horizonai.com, eng+pilot@horizonai.com, kevin@horizonai.com
- IPs to whitelist: we'll confirm the CIDRs shortly (our infra team is compiling them).
- Test data: attaching a small anonymized prompt set (see attachment: horizon_pilot_requirements.pdf).

Please provision the temporary API key and send the SSO invites once ready. Also can you confirm whether the key will be scoped to a single model and whether there are token limits we should be aware of?

Thanks — Marta
